entities.name: Quincey the Bandit King

meta.lore: The 'King' of the bandits, once heralded as a hero of the common people in Dunley. His lack of proper reverence for the Church of Luminance saw him driven into Farbane, where his prowess in battle earned the respect of the banditry and, eventually, a place as their champion and king. He may have been a good man, once.
meta.fightGuide:
Double Swipe - His basic melee attack consists of 2 swipes with his mace.
Shock Wave - After a brief charge, he'll do a knockback melee attack that inflicts a minor  debuff. He'll then create 4 waving shockwave lines that explode after a couple seconds that also inflict the lesser . Stacks with regular .
Mace Throw - He throws his weapon, tracking player movement and snaring them if it hits.
Chaos Barrier - He shouts "Show me what you've got!" and creates a reflective shield that inflicts  if hit. The shield does not deflect AoE attacks such as  or the crossbow's Rain of Bolts.
Summon Minion - He shouts "Rise to the challenge!" and spawns a Trapper.
Merciless Charge - His shield will shine for a second before he does a charge attack that does heavy damage and stuns.
Triple Charge - At half health he shouts "A rousing battle!" and does 3 charges in a row. He'll be briefly stunned afterwards.

entities.name: Rufus the Foreman

meta.lore: A lieutenant of the bandit forces charged with looking over the logging camp. Just because he's an expert woodworker doesn't mean he doesn't know his way around a crossbow, though. He didn't rise up in the bandit ranks for nothing.
meta.fightGuide:
Crossbow Bolt - Rufus' standard attack. He fires a crossbow bolt with a red glow in a straight line.
Throw Net - Much like the Trapper ability, Rufus swings a net around before throwing it into the AoE indicator. Any player still in that zone when he throws the net will be pinned in place for several seconds.
Dodge Roll - If the player draws too close to him he can dodge-roll away.
Summon Minions - Rufus calls for some minions, a Thug and a Poacher, to join the fight.
Rage - Rufus will shield himself and any of his nearby allies, similar to the Blood Rage ability.
Rapid Crossbow - Once Rufus gets to about half health he says "I'm gonna call you target practice!" and fires 8 crossbow bolts in rapid succession. After that the weapon will clinck, indicating to the player that the attack is over.

entities.name: Sir Erwin the Gallant Cavalier

meta.lore: Sir Erwin is an expert horseman, known both for his skill on horseback and unbearable company at formal events. Being generally disliked by his superiors but too skilled and devoted to the Light to exile to Farbane, he was instead sent to prepare for a grand offensive against the Cult of the Damned. Atop his fearless steed, Charger, he trains at the Dunley Horse Track, waiting for his promised troops. Surely, they'll arrive any day now.
meta.fightGuide:
Erwin fights on horseback, granting him significant movement speed.
Swipe - His basic melee attack consisting of a delayed horizontal swing with his sword. This attack has low range but swings in a wide arc.
Twin Lightning - He shouts "Twin Lightning!" or "Spears of Glory!" and fires 2 Ball Lightning projectiles. These projectiles track where the player is moving and launch in that direction rather than directly at the player. He will sometimes cancel this ability early to use another one, resulting in only 1 or even 0 projectiles.
Holy Artillery - He shouts "Holy Artillery!" or "From the Heavens!" and 2 area of effect lightning blasts strike from the sky after a brief delay.
Stunning Leap - His horse leaps high into the air, then crashes down dealing lightning damage in a large area. Erwin is briefly stunned after landing.
Lightning Charge - He shouts "Bravely forward, Charger!", "Sally forth!", or "Charge!!!" and charges at the player, stunning them if he hits.
Hyper Charge - His horse rears up on its hind legs, he raises his sword in the air, shouts "Charger, I think I've got it!", "Charge like thunder!", or "The Heavens are on my side!" and charges toward the player while small lightning bolts strike in a wave that follows his charge.

meta.lore: A fanatical servant of the Church of Luminance, his blind faith in the Light makes him the perfect candidate for Overseer of the Silver Mines. He is willing to look past the vile actions of the church, and even enforce them if it's in the interest of what he believes is the greater good. Even if it means doing something he might never condone, such as forced labor, or exiling his beloved daughter.

entities.name: Solarus, o Imaculado

meta.lore:
A legendary paladin of the Light and the oldest living member of the Church of Luminance. He has watched firsthand the descent of mankind with disinterest. A pioneer from the age of heroes, he remembers the struggle of facing down Dracula’s armies until all hope was lost. He remembers finding the light... He remembers the satisfaction of lifting his holy blade to the Immortal King, and striking down the greatest evil the world has ever seen.
He yearns to return to the days where he knew glory.
meta.fightGuide:
Solarus the Immaculate has three phases. It is recommended for multiple players to attempt this fight together, but can still be accomplished solo, albeit with more difficulty.

It is highly advised for the player to use the full Bloodmoon Armour set, a sanguine or ancestral weapon of their choosing and an upgrade of the Blood Merlot Amulet. For weapons, a reaper with it's Howling Reaper ability can do a lot of damage to Solarus as he frequently stands still during both his buzzsaw attacks as well as his Luminance attack. For abilities, counters and blocks are always good defensive options. Abilities that are hard to hit usually, such as  or , are worth considering as they are easier to hit for the same reason Howling Reaper is easy to hit. Lastly,  can usually deal its full damage to Solarus as the majority of the fight he will be isolated, though the player should wait until The Fallen Angel in phase 3 dies to use this again.

General tips: The fight with Solarus can be seen as a mix of the fights with Gorecrusher the Behemoth and The Winged Horror, which prior to the Gloomrot update preceded him. Like with Gorecrusher, Solarus' attacks reward the player for making more aggressive choices, such as using their Travel Ability to go towards the boss rather than away from them, this being discussed later. Furthermore, Solarus covers a lot of area both with his projectile attacks and his phase 2 and phase 3 beams of light, similarly to The Winged Horror. Lastly, during phase 3, the Fallen Angel should be hit as little as possible unless the player desperately needs healing and their only way of getting any is through life leeching effects. The best course of action is to let Solarus kill the angel while you attack him from afar. That said, Solarus will still sometimes attack the player rather than the angel so it is advised to remain cautious.

phases.title: Phase 1
phases.body:
Buzzsaw - Solarus will perform a slow, wide swing in front of himself before chopping down while firing a buzzsaw projectile. After travelling for a while, the buzzsaw will split in two, one going to the left and one to the right, before returning towards Solarus, converging in front of him.
Light Wave - Solarus will spawn a large amount of projectiles on either side of him that, forming two semicircles as they spread out, with a small amount of space between each projectile.
Charge - Solarus will prepare to charge, aiming ahead of where the player is moving in an attempt to intercept them. In the wake of his charge, projectiles will be fired on either side of him in a tight formation. If Solarus hits the player he will deal damage and stun the player.
Luminance - Starting at around 70% health, Solarus will go into the middle of the arena, shout "This is luminance", and spawn two light vortexes, one to his left and one to his right. The vortexes each shoot 3 projectiles in a spiraling pattern. The vortexes fire at slightly different angles.
Divine Angel - At 50% health, Solarus will summon a Divine Angel to assist him in battle. While the angel can be damaged during this phase it cannot be killed, becoming immune and beginning to regenerate if brought down to half health. During this time, the angel doesn't attack. As the angel is the focus of phase 2, it's attacks will be discussed there. The player will take damage in a small area around where the angel is summoned.

phases.title: Phase 2
phases.body:
This phase starts when Solarus is close to death during the first phase. Solarus will become immune to all damage and begin summoning beams of light that sweep across the arena, damaging everything they touch. On Brutal Solarus will also regen his health. This phase ends when the angel summoned in the first phase is killed. The angel's attacks are as follows:
Swipe Combo - The angel will quickly swipe twice in front of themselves before thrusting their spear forwards. The thrust shoots out several more thrusts forwards. If the player is too close to the angel, the thrusts will bypass block, damaging the player.
Charge - The angel will quickly charge forwards, dealing damage and knocking aside the player if the charge connects.
Bolts - The angel will begin shooting bolts of light that explode, dealing damage and knocking aside the player if they are caught in the area. The bolts will damage and knock the player aside even through block.
Empowered Light Wave - This attack is similar to Solarus' light wave, although the angel will fire more projectiles in an hourglass shape after the initial semicircle.

phases.title: Phase 3
phases.body:
After defeating the angel it will slowly be corrupted into a Fallen Angel. Once this is done, they will break Solarus' immunity and continue aiding the player during this phase until it dies. Solarus' gains new attacks in this phase while only losing his melee attack from last phase, it being replaced with a stronger version.
Buzzsaw Combo - Solarus will quickly slash in front of himself three times before slashing downwards, firing two buzzsaws in a V pattern in front of himself. As expected, each buzzsaw will split into two then return to Solarus.
Light Beams - Solarus will summon beams of light to sweep across the arena, which are identical to the ones from phase 2. The beams will linger for a while, becoming a threat during Solarus' other attacks.
Leap - Solarus will leap at the player, dealing damage in a wide array around himself as he lands. If the player is hit by the leap they will become incapacitated. Solarus will always follow up the leap with heavy swing that does high damage and throws the player backwards. The leap cannot be countered or blocked.

phases.title: Phase 1
phases.body:
Buzzsaw: The player can safely walk out of the swing range of Solarus before sidestepping the buzzsaw. Afterwards, if the player walks unto the very tip of Solarus' sword, or slightly above, then they should be safe from the boomeranging buzzsaws. The player can also choose to get behind Solarus with their Travel Ability, as the buzzsaws do not cover any ground directly behind him. However, when using  this might become riskier as Solarus can turn fairly quickly after the swing and the Veil in question is, strangely, the only one that doesn't hide the player after the initial dash.
Light Wave: Using your Travel Ability to pass through the point where the two semicircles overlap is the safest way of dodging this attack. Alternatively, the player can use their Travel Ability to get right next to Solarus during this attack as it does not hit directly in front of him apart from the very start. This, however, is very risky. Alternatively the player can use a barrier of their choice, damaging Solarus or healing themselves in the process.
Charge: The first way to safely dodge this attack is moving either left or right while Solarus is preparing the attack. Then, when Solarus is about to charge, start moving in the opposite direction of where you were initially going while staying in front of the boss so as to not get hit by the bolts that come after the dash. The second way of dodging this attack is getting behind Solarus while he charges with your Travel Ability or to simply counter or block the charge.
Luminance: Staying as far away from the vortexes during this attack will give the player as much time to react to each bolt as possible. The player should also use this time to damage Solarus with ranged attacks. A good place to stay is the entrance to the arena.

phases.title: Phase 3
phases.body:
Unmentioned Attacks: These attacks have already been covered previously and are dodged in the same way as previously mentioned. The only attack that this doesn't apply to is the Buzzsaw attack as that one doesn't make an appearance during this phase.
Buzzsaw Combo: The initial swing comes out fast, combined with the fact that the following two swings leave no pause in between make countering, blocking or dashing away from Solarus the only reliable way of avoiding damage. As for the two buzzsaws, simply walking away from Solarus without going left or right will dodge the initial two buzzsaws and standing a a short distance away from Solarus' sword should also dodge the four boomeranging buzzsaws. The player can also dodge the buzzsaws if they are right next to them before splitting. Dashing behind Solarus still works, although the player should wait before revealing themselves so as to not let Solarus turn around.
Leap: The leap can be avoided with the Travel Ability. However, Solarus will always follow up with his wide swing which can do upwards of 100 damage meaning the player should avoid it at all costs. As such, after dodging the leap, the player should make as much distance between themselves and Solarus as possible, or to go behind him. If the leap connects with the player, there is no way of dodging the swing as the incapacitate effect will keep the player still for just long enough to get hit.

entities.name: Stavros the Carver

meta.lore: One will not expect a simple craftsman to be so vicious in battle, but none represent the Venom Blades' endless thirst for havoc and consumption better that Stavros. From carving the trees with runes of corruption to harvesting the Venom Sap those trees produce, he works with a cold glee. Whether it be bark or flesh, every cut of his knife is a show of his devotion to the great witch Megara. Like any Venom Blade, he loves and fears his queen in equal measure, revering her as a goddess and looking to her for higher purpose.

entities.name: Talzur the Winged Horror

meta.lore: A creature that was once one of Dracula’s favorite pets. The monster mourned the death of its master in a blood-soaked vigil, enduring the toxic, bloody rains that followed Dracula’s death for seven days and seven nights. Unlike the many creatures that suffered under the rains, this one embraced the agony. Through its love and devotion for the tyrant king, it was able to embrace all of the hatred passed down through the downpour’s curse and become The Winged Horror.
meta.fightGuide:
At first, due to the large amount of projectiles The Winged Horror has, all the burning ground some of these projectiles leave behind as well as it's very strong melee attacks, the fight can seem exceedingly hard. However, this fight rewards patience rather than aggression and, once the player realizes this, makes the fight the easiest one out of the endgame bosses.
Retreat - During the fight, The Winged Horror will retreat directly away from the player whenever they get close. This weirdly happens even if The Winged Horror itself gets close to the player instead of the other way around.
Debuffs - The Winged Horror fight features two unique debuffs. The first is a damage over time, applied by it's Chaos attacks and the second one slowing down the player, applied by it's Frost attacks. If the player is burning and gets hit with a frost attack the burning will be cleansed and the slowing effect will take effect, and vice versa. This makes it so the player can never be affected by both debuffs at the same time. The debuffs last for about 10 seconds each.
Projectiles - The Winged Horror's projectiles are either Chaos Volley style fireballs or Crystal Lance icicles, applying the burning and slowing debuffs respectively. The icicles in particular always split into two additional icicles, forming a Y pattern. These secondary icicles do not split further.
Fire Breath - The Winged Horror flies up and spews fire down to the ground in one spot for a few seconds. Fireballs will shoot out from the location of the stream. When the fireballs land they deal damage and scorch the ground. The player will take damage and be inflicted with the burning debuff if they step on the scorched ground.
Flare Charge - The Winged Horror will unfurl it's wings one at a time while also summoning a fireball on either side of it's body. Afterwards, it and the fireballs quickly charge towards the location it was facing, dealing damage to the player. If the player is hit by The Winged Horror instead of the fireballs, they will be pushed back and will very likely be attacked by a swipe. If the player is behind The Winged Horror, it is likely The Horror will attempt a Tail Whip instead. Later in the fight, the charge will spread scorched ground if it comes into contact with any.
Swipe and Tail whip - The Winged Horror swipes forwards with it claws or whips with it's tail. Both attacks deal damage in an arc while shooting a volley of icicles. The tail whip is used only when the player is behind The Winged Horror.
Spin - The Winged Horror curls up before spinning in place, dealing damage around itself and knocking back players while firing icicles all around itself.
Fireball Drop - Starting at around 70% health, The Winged Horrror will fly up and across the battlefield while dropping fireballs that scorch the earth. Once it's done dropping fireballs, The Horror will violently crash back down to the arena. As the fight progresses, The Horror will do multiple flights over the battlefield, each with it's own set of fireballs.
Frost Vortex - Starting at around 70% health, The Winged Horror will roar, causing snow to build up in an area. Shortly afterwards, a blizzard will appear in the area, dealing damage to players inside.
Fireball Volley 1 - Starting at around 50% health, The Winged Horror will breathe 4 sets of fireballs in a semi-circle in front of itself. The first and third set of fireballs are lighter in color and have consistent speed while the second and fourth set have darker and move at different speeds, causing them to cover the space between the first and third set's space in between the fireballs. The fireballs leave behind scorched earth when they disappear.
Fireball Volley 2 - Starting at around 30% health, The Winged Horror will spawn 2 Chaos vortexes on either side of itself and begin violently batting it's wings, causing a strong gust of wind. The player is pushed back constantly by the wind while the vortexes shoot fireballs towards the player. The batting of it's wings will also spread scorched earth if any is caught in the area.

Due to this being an endgame boss, be prepared with a Bloodmoon Armour set, Amulets magic source and Sanguine tier weapons. More specifically, the best weapons for this fight are ranged weapons such as pistols or crossbows or those that have ranged abilities such as axes and Reapers.
This fight can be attempted at a lower gear level with patience if you stay at range the whole time. For that purpose, ranged abilities such as Sanguine Coil or Chaos Volley are ideal. Using spells with jewels that cleanse debuffs is also an excellent defensive option. Lastly, unholy spells that summon allies should be avoided as they will cause The Horror to use melee attacks much more often.
Scholar Blood is the ideal blood type for this fight as the bulk of your damage should be done via abilities, with another option being Brute Blood for it healing capabilities and +1 Gear Level. If you want extra burst survivability, go for Warrior Blood.

General Tips: As previously mentioned, keeping your distance is the best strategy for this fight. This is due to the fact that The Winged Horror's Swipe and Tail Whip should be avoided at all costs as well as The Winged Horror itself retreating if you attempt to get close. If you start burning, it is beneficial to get close to the icicles from The Horror's other attacks, such as it's spin, so that you stop taking continuous damage, the slow being rather negligible.
Unmentioned attacks: Aside from the Swipe and Tail Whip, all the unmentioned attacks have obvious circle markers where they damage the player. Thusly, there isn't much detail to go into. As for Swipe and Tail Whip, The Winged Horror should never be in range to perform these attacks.
Flare Charge: There is a small space between The Horror and it's fireballs where the player can stand to safely dodge the attack. That said, using your Travel Ability or other defensive abilities such as counters or barriers is a safe way of avoiding this attack. The ability used will most likely be available again by the time of the next charge as The Horror doesn't perform this attack often.
Fireball Volley 1: The player should be cautious while dodging this attack. While it is easier to dodge by keeping distance between you and The Horror, do not go too far back otherwise you'll find yourself on scorched earth. As for the attack itself, you can slip between the fireballs when they don't overlap, as well as dash through them or use a counter or barrier ability.
Fireball Volley 2: The gust of wind that knocks the player back is in a cone shape and the fireballs will only be shot in that cone. As such, it is possible to escape the cone, dodging all the fireballs in the process.

sections.title: Other notes
sections.body:
There seems to be a limit as to how much scorched earth can be present at any given time.
When icicles split they explode in a small radius. This explosion deals no damage to the player but does debuff them with the slowing debuff, making it a way of cleansing the damage overtime debuff.
Due to the arena being on a mountain peak with very little shade, the fight will likely be abandoned if it becomes daytime unless The Winged Horror is nearly defeated.
While in the air, The Winged Horror cannot be hit.

If you start burning, it is beneficial to get close to the icicles from The Horror's other attacks, such as it's spin, so that you stop taking continuous damage, the slow being rather negligible.

Unmentioned attacks: Aside from the Swipe and Tail Whip, all the unmentioned attacks have obvious circle markers where they damage the player. Thusly, there isn't much detail to go into. As for Swipe and Tail Whip, The Winged Horror should never be in range to perform these attacks.

Flare Charge: There is a small space between The Horror and it's fireballs where the player can stand to safely dodge the attack. That said, using your Travel Ability or other defensive abilities such as counters or barriers is a safe way of avoiding this attack. The ability used will most likely be available again by the time of the next charge as The Horror doesn't perform this attack often.

Fireball Volley 1: The player should be cautious while dodging this attack. While it is easier to dodge by keeping distance between you and The Horror, do not go too far back otherwise you'll find yourself on scorched earth. As for the attack itself, you can slip between the fireballs when they don't overlap, as well as dash through them or use a counter or barrier ability.

Fireball Volley 2: The gust of wind that knocks the player back is in a cone shape and the fireballs will only be shot in that cone. As such, it is possible to escape the cone, dodging all the fireballs in the process.

entities.name: Terrorclaw the Ogre

meta.lore: A creature whose story has long since been lost to the ages, thought not without resemblance to some few legendary creatures that were once men. One cannot help but wonder what strange corruption has taken root in Vardoran.
meta.fightGuide:
Swipe - Terrorclaw swipes in front of him, then slams forward, freezing.
Charge - Terrorclaw roars, then leaps forward and bites.
Slam - Terrorclaw slams the ground, creating three lines of ice. After a delay, icicles appear on the lines, freezing. Ice Block/Phantom Aegis can be used to MITIGATE the damage received if a dodge/side step is not an option for you or a teammate.
Roar - Terrorclaw roars, incapacitating nearby enemies.
Icicles - Terrorclaw slams the ground multiple times, causing icicles to be dropped on the ground. These block most of his abilites.
Throw ice - Terrorclaw picks up a icicle, then throws to the player stunning on hit. This projectile pierces icicles on the ground. Looks to be intercepting (aimed toward a location which would hit if the target kept moving in the same direction). This attack can be fully parried with abilities such as Blood Rite, abilities such as Ward Of The Damned will NOT work(Ward of the Damned appears to work as of the Gloomrot update).
Freezing breath - Terrorclaw glows blue-white, then releases two waves in a large cone, freezing. The damage scales with proximity. This attack is blocked by icicles.
Arctic leap - Terrorclaw leaps in the air, slamming down in a large area dealing AoE damage.Upon landing, 4 novas of frost radiate out from the center, freezing.

entities.name: Tristan, o Caçador de Vampiros

meta.lore: A cold-blooded killer, and the scion of a long line of vampire hunters. Few are as prepared to face the rising tide of vampire threat as Tristan, and his drive to exterminate the last of the unholy threat is second to none.
meta.fightGuide:
Flaming strike - He coats his sword with fire and then swipes forward in an overhead swing after a short delay. This attack lights the player on fire if it hits them.
Icy swing - He coats his sword with ice and then immediately sweeps it in a wide arc in front of him that inflicts . He often uses this as a follow-up attack after Flaming strike.
Lunge - He leaps forward while thrusting his sword. This attack briefly snares the player if it hits them, but can be blocked by counter or shield abilities.
Flaming Crossbow - He draws his crossbow and fires a flaming bolt at the player. If the bolt hits the player, a minion, or the environment it will detonate and light a large area of the ground on fire. If blocked by a shield spell or countered, the bolt will disappear without leaving a flame patch.
Fire Bombs - He throws a fire bomb in the air which explodes into 5 separate bombs, lighting the ground on fire for several seconds when they land. He will often follow up this attack by firing his crossbow immediately afterwards.

meta.lore: A stalwart champion of law and order in Dunley, it's his mission to protect the common people with his chilling gifts. Some say his methods have been getting more harsh and violent ever since his sister was banished.
meta.fightGuide:
Double Swipe - His basic melee attack consists of 2 swipes with his mace that inflict .
Frost Barrier - He creates a reflective shield that radiates a cone of frost damage which inflicts  if hit. The shield does not deflect AoE attacks such as  or the crossbow's Rain of Bolts.
Crystal Lance - He holds his shield in the air, then swipes it in front of him, firing 5 ice projectiles in a cone that inflict . This ability is signaled by a distinct shrill sound effect.
Chill Charge - He shouts "I feel a chill coming on!" and gains increased movement speed as well as ice particles around his feet. After running back and forth for a moment he will charge toward the player and inflict  if he hits them, then repeat this process 2 more times.

entities.name: Voltatia the Power Master

meta.lore: The trusted Right Hand of Doctor Henry Blackbrew, Voltatia is responsible for the maintenance and protection of the entire electric pipeline of Gloomrot, providing the region with their much needed energy supply. A stern professional and born leader, Voltatia operates with psychotic efficiency, and has little emotional desire beyond keeping The Doctor's operation running smoothly.

phases.title: Phase 1 - (100%-81%)
phases.body:
Electro Ray - This is her main attack, used in any proximity. Voltatia will stop and charge her cannon for 1.5s, after which she will track your position and fire for 2.5-3s. This attack is best side-stepped, ensure you're moving while she charges her cannon. Parry spells such as Blood Rite will not work not even for one tick, neither will shield spells such as Ward of the Damned, damage can however be mitigated with absorption spells such as Ice Block but cannot be fully absorbed without a top-tier spell power build. I recommend not wasting your dodge on this attack unless there's 2 Voltatias shooting from 2 very different angles. Rage spells such as Power Surge can help very much with its increased movement speed to easily side step this attack and do some damage. All dodge abilities such as Veil of Chaos will fool Voltatia to shoot the figure you leave behind, allowing you to throw a Vermin Salve or Blood Rose Brew down the gullet to keep 100% health during the first two less intense phases.
Electro Shotgun - This is her preferred close proximity attack, she will morph her cannon in a wider nozzle for 1s and shoot once in a cone fashion multiple bullets. This attack has several counters. If you are in melee range then you could side step it by circling her if you do it right. The attack can be parried with spells such as Blood Rite, it can also be blocked with spells like Ward of the Damned, damage can be fully absorbed with Ice Block if you have spell power ~40, Phantom Aegis is weaker in strength, it will not fully absorb - you'll need spell power over 50 which is hard without a dedicated spell power build.
Teleport - Voltatia will infuse with electricity and teleport to another location. You could use Polarity Shift if you want to stay close to her for melee damage, although keep in mind you have finite active spell slots, might not be worth it for your play style.
Electric dome - Voltatia will generate a dome of electricity and turn invisible and run to reposition to attack you. If you are inside the dome, it will not cause any damage, it will simply push you a few steps back. The dome does not block projectiles. While doing this ability she becomes briefly immobile, creating an opportunity to use a spell like Void or Corrupted Skull for some extra damage

phases.title: Phase 2 - (80%-61%)
phases.body:
Minion summon - She will stop and shout for help, summoning 2 Railgunners. They are comparatively weak, just keep them in mind and hit them when you can, they have static aim so they are easy to dodge, they will also make a mini-shotgun and blast you if you're too close and unlucky but it doesn't deal as much damage as Voltatias shotgun. Any offensive spell works against them as they move around a lot and long range hits will be a boon against them.
Lightning curtain - she will place down a fence of electricity and stand behind it using her electro ray to deal damage. In this state she is static, therefore any target area spell such as Void can be used to summon damage right next to her. Projectile spells such as Chaos Volley will NOT work, it will be absorbed by the fence, even Chaos Barrage, an ultimate ability, can't get through. If you touch this barrier you will receive damage, the only way to get past this fence is to either walk around it or dash through it using your dodge to apply melee damage.

phases.title: Phase 3 - (60%-41%)
phases.body: Clone - Voltatia will bash her weapon multiple times and phase out, after which 2 Voltatias will attack you for the remainder of the fight. Until now you've been fighting on easy mode, forget healing, forget using dash whenever you want, keep side stepping, keep using your spells to damage and use melee damage as you move better with melee, keep your main weapon and have the Sanguine Slashers on standby too - use the slashers ability Camouflage to turn invisible in order to reposition and try a different angle, especially if you're stuck in a bad position. try to keep your dodge as movement towards Voltatia and prioritise ending the battle quickly from now, I recommend using Veil of Chaos as it allows you to double dodge and get further. Hitting any Voltatia damages the other too, so hit any Voltatia you can. I also recommend using Potion of Rage and Witch Potion to increase your spell damage/shield and primary damage too.

phases.title: Phase 4 - (40%-0%)
phases.body: Electro disc - Voltatia will lower herself and activate her back device which will throw ricocheting electric discs at you. This move is best countered with a combination of sidestepping, parry and dodge if it allows you to get near a Voltatia to damage her. For this move there is no one strategy which is better than the other, but dodging into the wave of discs to get to the Voltatia behind seems like the more favourable strategy because it allows you to go on the offensive instead of the defensive, so Veil of Chaos is best.

entities.name: Willfred the Village Elder

meta.lore: An honored and deeply respected chief of a small, reclusive village of outcasts. Despite the imminent threat of the Cult of the Damned, dangerous wildlife, and even the rumor of Werewolves stalking northern Dunley, he manages to keep his people fed and happy.
meta.fightGuide:
Swipe - Willfred will swipe at you up to 2 times. This is extended if he hits both swipes, or cut short if you leave his range.
Rage - Willfred glows red, walks towards you quickly, and bites at you 3 times in quick succession.
Lunge - Willfred gets on all fours and prepares to lunge at you. This will inflict a 3 second stun and deal heavy damage as he shouts "Hold still".
Heart Strike - Willfred will turn invisible and encircle his prey. On Brutal Difficulty, Willfred will also summon a Frost Wolf for every player in combat. When he reveals himself again, Willfred will lunge at you with an attack that inflicts the Heart Strike debuff, This explodes and deals damage after 3 seconds. This attack's application and explosion cannot be countered, only evadedIf an invulnerability effect is active when the effect expires, such as that from a successful counter or a dash, no damage will be taken. Occasionally Willfred will summon a copy of himself, which also performs Heart Strike once in close proximity. This appears to trigger randomly.Citation needed
When Willfred drops below 50% health for the first time, he'll howl and release a number of PrisonersLikely scaling with player count from the three cages around his 'arena'. When Willfred shouts "Let me have a taste" Willfred will try to eat one of them to restore his health. If Willfred successfully consumes a villager, Willfred will HealPotentially Exclusive to Brutal difficulty and  Rage - running at the player. It is advised to kill as many prisoners as you can before Willfred consumes them.

sections.title: Overview

sections.body:

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: Shadowbolt is a spell with heavy damage, but also a long cast time that makes you vulnerable to enemy spells. The ability is great when combined with some kind of crowd control, like the stun from , incapacitate from Axes'  or a  effect. Best cast after an enemy has used all defensive spells.

It was nerfed in 1.0 Hotfix #6 the following ways:
Stun duration reduced to 0.6s from 0.8s.
Jewel that allows you to recast, damage reduced from 25 - 50% to 15 - 30% and knockback effect power reduced by ~25%.
Jewel increasing stun duration reduced from 0.2 - 0.4s to 0.1 - 0.3s.
Jewel granting immaterial, duration reduced from 0.8 - 1.6s to 0.8 - 1.2s

The immaterial jewel was removed.
Targets triggering the counter are no longer subjected to the stun or knockback effect if they're immaterial when the trigger happens. Static is still inflicted.
The recast jewel now inflicts a fading snare rather than knockback (no longer interrupting casts).

sections.body:
Soulburn was added with the release of V Rising's first expansion, Secrets of Gloomrot on May 17th, 2023.
It was unlocked upon defeating Lord Styx the Night Champion.
It had a cooldown of , a cast time of , and the following effect:

The spell could instantly cancel almost all non-counter player spells and weapon skills. If none were cancelled immediately, a unique "Spell Block" debuff would automatically cancel the player's next spell or weapon skill cast for ~0.7s, including primary attacks. Only if something was cancelled would the silence trigger.
Over the years it was subjected to two nerfs:

In [https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1604030/view/3657533302488647084 Gloomrot Hotfix #7] its silence duration was nerfed from 2.5s to 1.5s.

In Update 1.0 its cast time was nerfed from 0.2 to 0.5s.

Finally, in Update 1.1 it was reworked into its current iteration.

sections.title: Soul Shard Mechanics
sections.body:
Upon equipping the jewelry, the player's ultimate ability is replaced with :

"Become invulnerable and channel a Blood Storm for 3s, launching up to 25 homing blood bolts at nearby enemies. Each bolt deals 100% magic damage and inflicts . End with a powerful nova, dealing 300% magic damage and pushing enemies away."

In Update 1.1. players may replace the Soul Shard's ultimate ability freely.

The damage bonus to vampires applies to both players and enemies.

 increases movement speed, damage output, attack speed, and life leech by 15% for 6 seconds.

Soul Shards lose durability over time and can only be repaired by feeding on Primal Blood Souls during Tier 2 Rift Incursions. Each Primal Blood Soul consumed restores 750 durability, distributed between all shards in the player's inventory. If a Soul Shard is destroyed it returns to its V Blood Carrier, in this case Dracula.
After Update 1.1 its durability loss may now be sped up or disabled via the Server Settings.

They may be teleported outside of raid windows, and carried while in . (toggleable in settings)

On PvP servers Soul Shards are dropped on death, and can be stolen by other players. To prevent this, they may be stored in their respective pedestals; .

Soul Shards are automatically destroyed if not picked up from the ground within 60 minutes.

sections.title: Notes
sections.body:
Lunge was reworked in the October patch to deal 90% physical damage from 120%, but can now be recast once on hit. And post cast duration reduced to 0.3s.
The recast remains available even while swapped to a different weapon.
Skewering Leap Incapacitate duration was increased to 1.2s from 1.0s, and the self-stun duration on miss was reduced to 0.45s from 0.7s.

infobox.style: "text-align: left" |Fire a quick bolt that deals 75% physical damage, interrupts attacks, inflicts Marked and inflicts a 1.5s fading snare. The bolt splits into two upon hit.

sections.title: Mechanics
sections.body:
After consuming 3 marks, Crossbow's primary attack DPS increases to 78%, excluding mark proc damage - the highest in the game.
The increased attack speed bonus from Marked applies to all Crossbow Skills.
Rain of Bolts has a random delay before impact between 0.9s - 1.4s.
The Snapshot splitting bolts appear to have a very minor tracking behaviour, allowing them to more reliably hit enemies.

infobox.style: "text-align: left" |Inflict a 1.5s fading snare and release all nearby daggers that are stuck in the ground. Released daggers return to you, piercing enemies and dealing 40% physical damage. Each dagger that returns grant one dagger stack and reduces the cooldown of Rain of Daggers by 0.2s.

sections.title: Mechanics
sections.body:
The Throw Daggers description is slightly misleading. You will always have a minimum of one dagger to throw, even without waiting the full 1.1 second. In practice this make the actual cooldown closer to the listed 0.55 seconds. This also means deliberately only casting Throw Daggers at max stacks results in a significant DPS loss.
Dagger stacks can be gained and expended freely during the Throw Dagger cast time. However, the dagger stack cooldown resets at the end of the Throw Dagger cast time.
For example, if you were to start casting Throw Dagger immediately upon reaching 2 stacks, the 0.6+ seconds of stack regeneration gained during the cast animation will be lost once you run out of daggers to throw.
Simply holding down the attack input for Throw Daggers will result in near zero stack regeneration loss and optimal DPS output by default, if no attack speed bonuses are applied.
However, minimizing stack regeneration loss in-between other Weapon Skills and Spells is tricky. It requires precise timing of your dagger throw such that the last dagger stack is gained right as you're running out of daggers to throw. If you undershoot the timing, even more stack regeneration will be lost.
Throw Dagger will only leave a dagger on the ground if it hits a target or solid object.
Release Daggers can be animation cancelled at any point, and all daggers will still return to the player.
The returning daggers from Release Daggers won't pierce solid objects.
The player is invincible during the leap of Rain of Daggers.
Its unique bursty combo design and its ability to gain additional daggers from the Release Daggers skill makes a calculation of the primary skill's DPS in isolation unreflective of its actual damage output. When optimized, this weapon has some of the highest damage potential in the game.

sections.title: Pistol Mechanics
sections.body:
Much like other weapons, you can weave abilities in between your primary combo attacks.
But unlike other weapons, the pistols only have a significant cast time for the first attack in the combo.
This makes the final two shots able to be weaved in much more seamlessly than the first.
In the 1.1 October patch Explosive Bullet's explosion damage was reduced to 115% from 125%, and Fan the Hammer was slightly reworked:
Can now move at 35% speed while channeling the attack.
Channeling duration reduced to 1.3s from 1.5s (increasing firing rate).
Cone size reduced by ~50% making the spread less random.
Reduced the knockback on bullet hit slightly.

sections.title: Mechanics
sections.body:
Elusive Strike has a range of 6.5 meters.
Camouflage doesn't apply full invisibility, there's a slight blur effect overlayed on the character.
Elusive Strike fading snare duration was reduced to 1.5s from 2s in the 1.1 October patch.

infobox.style: "text-align: left" |Throw a spear that deals 110% physical damage, pulls the enemy towards you and inflict a 1.5s fading snare.

sections.title: Mechanics
sections.body:
A Thousand Spears has diminishing returns, stacking up to 10 times and making the target immune for up to 7s. A full attack may inflict 8 stacks. The recast does not inflict any stacks and is unaffected by the diminishing returns.
A Thousand Spears was nerfed in the 1.1 October patch the following ways:
Reduced the move distance when stepping forward during the cast to 1.25 from 2.
Increased cooldown to 9s from 8s.
Increased Thrust recast time to 0.3s from 0.25s.

infobox.style:
"text-align: left" |Send forth a shockwave dealing 100% physical damage and launching the enemy hit into the air for 1.6s.
Recast the ability to teleport to the target striking it three times, each strike dealing 20% physical damage.
"text-align: left" |Lunge forward and swing your twinblade dealing 100% physical damage in a line and launching enemies into the air and to the opposite side of you.

sections.title: Notes
sections.body:
Javelin recast does not trigger counters.
Also doesn't trigger Ancestral Spell School effects unless explicitly stated.

sections.title: Notes
sections.body: Vampiric Curse is a debuff that deals damage and heals the user once it expires after 3 seconds. The curse explosion can be avoided by going immaterial, such as when using a Veil Spell.
